correctness.rationale: Re-audited the narrowed least-brightness statement. The facet vectors give 2c+max(c,ha)+max(c,hb) in the unsigned octant. At fixed c in [0,1/4] the unit-sublevel polygon has each scaled horizontal coordinate ≤1−3c and sum ≤1−2c. Its five listed corners are affine in c, so all slice points are in the convex hull of the endpoint slices. Of the seven resulting points only the horizontal axial pair and (1/(4h),1/(4h),1/4) can have largest Euclidean norm. Strict convexity excludes mixtures, and homogeneity gives the reciprocal minimum and all equality directions, with tie only at h²=14. Near a horizontal minimizer the linear cusp 2|z|+max(|z|,h|y|) has unit sublevel area (4/h)∫₀^(1/3)(1−2z)dz=8/(9h), and the local sphere Jacobian tends to one. At the oblique minimizer put D=h²+2 and p=hU₁−U₃, q=hU₂−U₃. The gradient cross product dotted with the unit normal is h√D and dU₃=−(dp+dq)/D. Thus α=4/D and 1−α are the positive directional weights; summing four triangles gives area 1/[2α²(1−α)²]. Multiplying the chart Jacobian and the 4 or 8 sign copies and dividing by sphere area 4π gives the reported coefficients, with oblique weight eight times horizontal at √14. For h=√14+λε the competing heights have slope difference 7/8, giving the two separate positive-part budgets. Uniform coercive cusp expansions localize each rescaled chart to bounded sets, and the limiting level boundaries have area zero even at zero residual budget. This justifies the limits for every fixed x≥0 and λ, including their zero and tie cases.
residual_risks: Proof is analytic; the original finite projection checker neither certifies exhaustiveness of the vertex proof nor proves limiting probabilities. Corrected laws assume the centered right square and uniform orthographic orientations.

value.rationale: The question is which views of a basic polyhedral solid give the least projected area and how often a uniform view nearly attains that extremum. At a natural aspect-ratio threshold the minimizing views change from horizontal axes to oblique directions with two active facet switches, and their local neighborhoods contribute very unequal masses at coexistence. The exact coefficients and crossover quantify that geometry, including the rare-event budgets for heights differing on the error scale; they are not a renormalization of width or of upper spherical caps.
residual_risks: No generalization beyond the stated pyramid and sampling law is claimed; the two separate equations for upper and lower endpoints are not counted as a new joint classification.
